avt.anchorFacts.heldDescription: These extractions are genuinely uncertain in meaning — the content is provisional or unconfirmed, not merely written by hand. They are held out of scoring until a reviewer confirms, edits, or retypes them. A legible source is never queued just for its medium.

avt.claimDetail.interpretationCaveat: A contributing fact carries a substantive interpretation caveat — what the evidence means, not the medium it came in, is what is uncertain.
avt.claimDetail.notVerifiable.reopenExpl: Set aside as not verifiable. If this is actually a checkable claim, re-open it: AVT keeps your reclassification and runs only the record-check it skipped.
avt.claimDetail.notVerifiable.reopenedPe: Re-opened as a checkable claim. It shows as No coverage until the document is verified again.

avt.claimDetail.note.placeholder: Record a correction or an explanation. Saving records the note against this claim only — it does not change the verdict or the anchor-fact record.
avt.claimDetail.overrideNotice: Overridden to {verdict} — the analysis below is the tool's own, shown unchanged.
avt.claimDetail.overrideTooltip: A reviewer has recorded a different verdict. The analysis below is the tool's own, unchanged.
avt.claimDetail.recordConflict.descripti: Two anchor facts speak to the same point — {subject} — but disagree. Both are high-confidence sources, so this is not a reliability problem: the record itself is internally inconsistent. AVT withholds a verdict rather than score the claim, because picking one record over the other is a judgement for you to make and record — not one the tool should make silently.
avt.claimDetail.recordConflict.escalated: Flagged for the evidence team. The record conflict stays open and counted until a governing record is chosen.
avt.claimDetail.recordConflict.governed: {value} governs: the claim is judged against this record. The other record stays on file.
avt.claimDetail.recordConflict.title: Conflicting evidence in the record
avt.claimDetail.reopenedTooltip: A reviewer re-classified this as a checkable fact; a live record check is still pending.
avt.claimDetail.score.noCoverage: The record is silent. No anchor fact in the database addresses this claim. This is distinct from a weak score — it means there is nothing to check it against yet.
avt.claimDetail.score.notVerifiable: Not a verifiable assertion. This is the kind of statement no document could ever settle — a counterfactual, a prediction, a statement of intent, a legal conclusion, or a claim too vague to check. Set aside rather than scored.
avt.claimTypes.fact.hint: Objective, checkable assertion — scored against the record. Includes claims framed as admissions or denials: judged on the underlying proposition, not the bare words.
avt.claimTypes.opinion.hint: A value judgement or characterisation — no document can confirm or contradict it, so it is set aside, not scored.
avt.claimTypes.opinion.label: Opinion
avt.claimTypes.unverifiable.hint: An assertion no document could ever settle — a counterfactual, a prediction, a statement of intent or belief, a legal conclusion, or a claim too vague to check. Set aside, not scored. Distinct from No coverage, which is a checkable fact the record is merely silent on.
avt.claimTypes.unverifiable.label: Not verifiable
avt.confidence.tooltip: Interpretive confidence — how unambiguous this evidence's meaning is. Independent of the source medium (handwriting, scan, etc.).
avt.disposition.contested: The verdict is clean, but a contributing fact's interpretation is contested — worth your eyes before sign-off.
avt.disposition.contradicted: The record departs from this claim. A human call is needed before this verdict stands.
avt.disposition.nocover: No anchor fact addresses this claim, so there's nothing to confirm it against. Sign-off is optional.
avt.disposition.notverifiable: Set aside as not verifiable — sign-off is optional. Re-open below if it's actually checkable.
avt.disposition.recordconflict: Two exhibits in the record disagree. Resolve which governs above, or flag the evidence team — the tool won't pick for you.
avt.disposition.supported: The record affirms this. Your sign-off confirms the tool read it correctly — no judgement call needed.
avt.disposition.tension: The record only partly supports this. Weigh the supporting and conflicting facts above before the verdict stands.

guides.help.title: Help and feedback
guides.nudge.body: New here? A few short tours show you around.
guides.tours.chat.description: Add context for AI and send your request securely
guides.tours.chat.examplePrompt: Summarize the key obligations in this contract
guides.tours.chat.steps.anonymize.body: Hides personal data before sending, then restores it in the answer.
guides.tours.chat.steps.anonymize.title: Send anonymized
guides.tours.chat.steps.anonymize.when: Turn it on when the text carries personal data and the question does not turn on who the parties are. Leave it off when identity is the point, such as a conflict check, because placeholders take away exactly what you are asking about.
guides.tours.chat.steps.attach.body: Uploads a file from this device into the conversation. It is read for this thread only and is not filed into a matter.
guides.tours.chat.steps.attach.title: Attach a file
guides.tours.chat.steps.attach.when: Best for a one-off document you do not need to keep: a draft that just arrived by email, a scan, a spreadsheet you only want summarized.
guides.tours.chat.steps.composer.body: Write what you want in plain language: the task, what it concerns, and the shape of answer you expect. Everything else here only sharpens a request you have already written.
guides.tours.chat.steps.composer.title: Start with the request
guides.tours.chat.steps.context.body: Adds an existing matter or file as context. Nothing is uploaded or copied.
guides.tours.chat.steps.context.title: Reference a matter or a file
guides.tours.chat.steps.context.when: Use this instead of attaching whenever the document is already filed. Reference the matter to let the assistant look across it; reference one file when you know exactly which one to read. Typing @ in an empty composer opens this list directly.
guides.tours.chat.steps.plusMenu.body: Use + to attach a file or reference a matter.
guides.tours.chat.steps.plusMenu.title: Add context with +
guides.tours.chat.steps.plusMenu.when: When the context you need is not yet in the chat.
guides.tours.chat.steps.send.body: Sends the message together with everything you attached, referenced, or switched on above. The composer stays put, so a follow-up can add whatever the first answer showed was missing.
guides.tours.chat.steps.send.title: Send it
guides.tours.chat.steps.send.when: The first answer shows what is still missing.
guides.tours.chat.title: Start with chat
guides.tours.chatPower.description: Use skills or connect other useful tools
guides.tours.chatPower.steps.mcp.body: Turns a connected server's tools on or off for your chats: business registries, internal systems, anything your team has connected.
guides.tours.chatPower.steps.mcp.title: Connected tool servers
guides.tours.chatPower.steps.mcp.when: Turn one on when the answer needs live data from outside the workspace. Leave the rest off: the fewer tools in play, the narrower and more predictable the answer.
guides.tours.chatPower.steps.models.body: Switches the model for this conversation only. Every other thread keeps the default set for your workspace.
guides.tours.chatPower.steps.plusMenu.bo: The same menu also holds the model switch, skills, and connected tool servers. The next steps open it and take each in turn.
guides.tours.chatPower.steps.skills.body: Inserts a saved prompt or a skill your team has written: a reviewed set of instructions that handles the same task the same way every time.
guides.tours.chatPower.steps.skills.when: Use one when the task repeats and the wording matters, such as a standard contract review or an intake summary. Typing / in an empty composer opens this list directly.
guides.tours.chatPower.title: Do more in chat
guides.tours.documents.description: File a document, then find it again
guides.tours.documents.steps.browse.body: This table is the matter's document list. Uploaded files land here as rows. To return later, open the matter from the sidebar, choose its table view, then select the document row.
guides.tours.documents.steps.upload.body: Upload opens the file picker; you can also drag files onto the matter. Each file becomes a document in this matter, where your team can find it and stella can use it in review.
guides.tours.documents.steps.upload.titl: File a document in the matter
guides.tours.documents.steps.upload.when: Upload here when the file belongs to the matter and should remain available. Attach it directly in chat only when it is temporary context for one conversation.
guides.tours.documents.title: Work with documents
guides.tours.playbooks.description: Save a document review process for next time
guides.tours.playbooks.steps.basics.body: Add a name and description. Limit it to a document type if needed.
guides.tours.playbooks.steps.overview.bo: A playbook keeps questions and rules for other documents.
guides.tours.playbooks.steps.positions.b: For each rule, choose whether to assess the text or extract a detail.
guides.tours.playbooks.title: Build a playbook
guides.tours.tabularReview.description: Extract answers across many files at once
guides.tours.tabularReview.steps.addColu: New column opens the column composer. Give the column a clear question-shaped name and tell stella exactly what to read for; the same instruction runs against every document row.
Ask one question of every document
Create a separate column for each answer you need to compare, filter, sort, or export. Keep related context in the prompt instead of combining several answers in one cell.
guides.tours.tabularReview.steps.answerT: Returns controls the shape of every answer. Choose a number, date, single select, or multi-select when the result has structure; stella will keep the column consistent instead of returning arbitrary prose.
Use select for a fixed set of outcomes, number or date for sorting and calculations, and text only when the answer genuinely needs narrative detail.
guides.tours.tabularReview.steps.table.b: Each row is a document; each custom column is one question asked of every document at once. That turns a folder of files into comparable answers without opening them one by one.
guides.tours.tabularReview.steps.table.t: Review the set, not one file
guides.tours.tabularReview.steps.table.w: Use the table when you need the same facts or decisions across several documents. Open a document directly when layout, wording, or surrounding context matters more than comparison.
guides.tours.tabularReview.title: Review in a table
guides.tours.workflows.description: Chain steps into a repeatable workflow
guides.tours.workflows.steps.create.body: Create opens an unsaved workflow draft. The next steps define when it starts, what it does, and where a person must decide whether it continues.
guides.tours.workflows.steps.overview.bo: A workflow connects a trigger to a sequence of actions, so a routine process runs the same way each time. It can prepare work automatically while keeping judgment with a reviewer where needed.
guides.tours.workflows.steps.overview.wh: Automate work that has a stable trigger, repeatable steps, and a clear owner for exceptions. Keep changing or judgment-heavy work manual until the process itself is settled.
A review gate pauses the run until a person approves or rejects it. Put the gate before the first action that should not happen solely on an automated result.
Use a gate before sending, filing, escalating, or otherwise committing a consequential result. Skip it only when the next step is safely reversible and needs no human judgment.
guides.tours.workflows.steps.steps.body: Steps run in this order and pass their work forward. Keep each step responsible for one clear action so failures are understandable and the sequence is easy to change.
guides.tours.workflows.steps.steps.title: Build the sequence
guides.tours.workflows.steps.trigger.bod: The trigger decides when a run begins: manually, on a schedule, or when matching files are uploaded. Narrow its matter and file conditions so unrelated work never starts the workflow.
guides.tours.workflows.steps.trigger.whe: Use manual while the process is new, a schedule for time-based routines, and file upload only when an arriving document is the reliable signal to begin.
guides.tours.workflows.title: Automate a workflow
